subject: Hosted API pricing: US vs EU delta + data residency premium
messages:
From: Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@acmehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing request — baseline + EU residency adder

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking a look — we're kicking off our vendor shortlist for Q3 and need a concise baseline for Redwood's hosted API pricing. Two asks: 1) what are the baseline per-token rates for the hosted text generation API in US regions (vCPU/GPU-backed fulfillment) and 2) what typical adder you apply for EU-hosting/data residency (we need to model FY28 budgets across regions).

We're especially interested in:
- Any explicit per-token multiplier or fixed monthly topology charge for EU-hosted variants
- Whether billing currency or invoice locality changes with residency (USD/EUR)
- If there are minimum commit tiers that materially change unit rates

Attached is our short RFP with expected volumes and compliance checklist (Acme_RFP_Q3.pdf). Can you send a one-pager or simple table we can plug into our procurement model? Ideally by EOD Friday.

Best,
Jordan Pike
Director, Platform Procurement
Acme Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing request — baseline + EU residency adder

Jordan —

Thanks for the RFP and the clear asks. Short version up front: we publish a unified hosted baseline and then apply a residency premium for EU-hosted instances to cover additional regional capacity and compliance controls. I've summarized the numbers below and attached our current public ratecard for reference (ratecard-hosted-2027.pdf).

Baseline hosted (public API) — Text gen (standard tokens):
- Pay-as-you-go: $0.0012 per token (USD)
- Monthly commit (>= $50k/mo): $0.00095 per token
- Enterprise reserved (negotiated): starts at $0.0007 per token depending on commit and term

EU residency premium options (applied on top of baseline):
- Soft residency (EU compute, global control plane): +8% unit adder
- Full VPC residency (EU compute + private control plane/hardened audit): +18% unit adder + $1,250/mo per-account topology charge
- Currency/invoicing: we can invoice in EUR for EU-only residency deals; exchange adjustments are applied at invoice time.

Notes on commits & structure:
- Commits are global by default but can be region-tagged for guaranteed EU capacity (affects pricing).
- For >$200k/month commitments we typically include a residency waiver for the topology charge.

Next steps — can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the RFP quickly? Marcus I"m looping you for commercial terms and Stephanie for invoice/currency specifics.

Action items for us:
- Marcus: prepare a quick excel (banded rates by commit) and a sample EU-invoice flow.
- Stephanie: confirm whether the topology charge can be credited at larger commits.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick screen share.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@acmehealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing request — baseline + EU residency adder

Jordan — quick follow from my side with an attached pricing sketch (acme-map-proposal.xlsx). Key clarifications:

- The +8% / +18% are unit multipliers on token pricing (not separate per-token line items). Example: PAYG US $0.0012 -> EU soft residency $0.001296.
- For modeling: assume topology charge only for full VPC residency; soft residency covers compute in-region but uses our shared control plane.
- For teams that want EUR invoicing: we'll issue a EUR invoice with the same numeric unit rates converted using the invoice date FX. We can hardcode a EUR price in the SOW if you need certainty.

I've penciled three scenarios in the attached:
1) PAYG with soft residency (no commit)
2) $75k/mo commit with partial EU-tagging (hybrid spread across regions)
3) $250k/mo enterprise reserved (EU capacity guaranteed, topology charge waived)

If those match your internal buckets, tell us which scenario to flesh out and Stephanie will produce a sample PO-ready invoice. Also happy to demo how the Console surfaces per-route regional usage to help your FinOps team.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing request — baseline + EU residency adder

Irene / Marcus —

This is really helpful, thanks. A couple quick clarifications from procurement:
- We think the soft residency (+8%) will work for our pilot phase (low latency not critical), but for production patient-facing workloads we will likely require full VPC residency. Can you confirm the SLO difference between the two?
- Is the topology charge a one-time setup or ongoing monthly? You mentioned $1,250/mo in the note — procurement prefers amortized setup fees if possible.

Next step: we'll pick scenario 2 (75k/mo) as our baseline for internal budget planning and would like a sample EUR invoice for that scenario so we can see how the numbers translate. If you can share the sample invoice and a 30-min slot tomorrow morning, we'll finalize which scenario to pursue.

I'll attach a quick internal cost model after the call.

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Platform Procurement
Acme Health
